acceptance_criteria.requirement: The wide dashboard uses min(1480px, calc(100vw - 64px)) with 24px top and 32px bottom margins.
The calendar and 430-450px statistics rail remain side by side at container widths of about 1220px and above.
Intermediate layouts place a full-width calendar above a two-by-two statistics grid and Bible card.
Narrow layouts use one statistics card per row, stacked controls and footer content, and no horizontal scrolling.
Month cells use a 44-50px release range, 5px gaps, readable dates, and no square-cell requirement.
Year uses an unframed wrapper up to about 940px, approximately 14px cells at wide geometry, and aligned month labels.
Year exposes Mon, Wed, and Fri reference labels and no new empty-state message.
Completed reviews own the cell fill, today owns one compact marker, and selection owns exactly one 2px outline.
Today, selection, completion, due workload, and event states can coexist without nested rings or halos.
Due presentation uses levels 0-3 with 2px, 4px, and 6px Month indicators plus compact Year indicators.
Events remain gold or orange across themes and multiple events receive a compact count treatment.
The legend says Completed reviews with Low and High endpoints and shows three matching due samples.
One delegated tooltip stays within the viewport at 220-260px and uses historical or future wording appropriate to the date.
Selected-date events use Event on this date; otherwise the global upcoming event uses Next event.
Footer event date, title, countdown, count and edit affordance stay grouped and long titles ellipsize safely.
Date actions use the exact labels Reviewed cards and Due cards, while Most missed remains conditional.
The statistics order remains Today’s Progress, Today’s Session, Last 7 Days, All Time in a stable two-by-two rail.
A true zero workload shows No cards due, omits the percentage, and leaves a neutral track.
Partial progress shows the numeric percentage alone, and completed nonzero work shows 100%.
Progress segments represent actual Completed, New, Learning, and Review counts with buried cards excluded.
Today’s Session always contains Cards studied, New cards studied, Time, Pace, and ETA.
Missing Pace or ETA renders an em dash, and Done appears only after a positive original workload reaches zero remaining.
Last 7 Days retains Retention and Again rate, and All Time retains Lifetime retention when values are unavailable.
Semantic category color applies only to positive values; zero is neutral and unavailable is muted.
Initial Python rendering and live JavaScript updates consume the same derived progress and session presentation state.
The Bible card remains beneath both statistics columns, preserves its font-size preference through a responsive clamp, and never truncates long verses.
Disabling the Bible card removes both the card and its layout gap.
Themes extend the existing semantic token layer and preserve stable cyan, amber, purple, gold and status colors.
Sapphire is the baseline, Graphite dark uses steel hierarchy, Emerald keeps routine values neutral, and High Contrast uses opaque crisp surfaces.
Default and native hosts receive no add-on-painted global canvas or root pseudo-surface.
A top-level scrim appears only when an actual or QA-injected background image is detected.
Configuration schema 7 retires study.show_eta and legacy ShowTimeLeft while preserving unrelated unknown keys and every other preference.
ETA remains a permanent Today’s Session row after migration.
Initial, delayed, failure, retry and fully loaded states are implemented and the dashboard cannot remain indefinitely in a skeleton.
Calendar view, calendar setting, theme, palette, visibility, events and Bible preferences survive an isolated restart without a dirty state.
The archive is rebuilt twice with identical checksum and passes allowlist, integrity, imports and source/archive parity.
The exact candidate runs only in a fresh sync-disabled disposable Anki 26.8.1 profile with verified process, profile, add-on, filesystem, window and disconnected-sync identity.
Sixteen distinct native Deck Browser frames cover every theme, mode and Month/Year combination at 100% text scale.
Supplemental tagged frames cover fresh and populated data, responsive states, calendar markers, footer relationships, backgrounds, Bible states, lifecycle and restart persistence.
The user-supplied screenshot and prior contact sheets remain calibration references and are never represented as newly generated evidence.
Dedicated 125% and 150% captures, spoken screen-reader review, Windows/Linux, forced colors and OS-level scaling remain explicitly deferred and unrun.
